I then have to tap the screen again just to bring it back up, which completely breaks my flow.

The same thing happens when I’m creating a list. If I hit enter to start a new line and pause for even a moment, the keyboard vanishes again. This happens constantly and makes something as simple as writing notes or lists way more difficult than it should be.

For a note-taking app, this is a major usability problem. Notes should be quick and effortless to edit, not an exercise in fighting the interface. Until this keyboard issue is fixed on iOS, Google Keep is honestly more frustrating than helpful.

title: One fatal flaw destroys accessibility
body:
It’s great to have it sync with family and Google Home.

But my primary use case is shared lists, and Keep has horrible accessibility.

On iOS, there is a three second timeout after which keyboard focus leaves a list item, finalizing the list item with whatever text was input. If you are a slow typer or use alternate input means - or even if you just need a few seconds to form your thoughts - google keep interrupts you.

You end up with empty list items because you didn’t type fast enough. You end up making multiple list items instead of one. You end up cut off with half written list items.

Unless you are a fast typer who always has fully formed thoughts ready to input without pause, this app is nearly unusable.

This no doubt demonstrates the limitations of a formulaic user testing process. I have a hunch that the Keep QA team has list entry items ready to go, and quickly runs through tests, rather than testing real world use cases - especially with a variety of accessibility considerations.
